editorial:
Imagine waking up in a gross, empty building with no idea how you got there, only to realize you are literally cooked. That is the wild setup you get here. You follow Barry, a guy struggling with a heavy drug habit, as he wanders through a dusty warehouse. The vibe is super gritty and weird, mixing a sad look at addiction with some really gross horror elements. It feels like a bad trip brought to life, where you are never quite sure if what you are seeing is real or just a memory flashing in his head before the end.

The acting is surprisingly solid, and the practical effects are the real star here since they look nasty in the best way possible. While the story moves a bit slow at first, the weird twists keep you interested. If you like movies that feel like a fever dream, you will love this. It is a short ride, but it leaves a big impression.
endingExplained: You eventually find out that Barry is actually dead. The whole movie is just his spirit reliving his final moments and his mistakes while his physical body is being used as food. The big twist is that he was killed and cooked by people who treat humans like livestock. By the end, he accepts his fate and realizes there is no going back, leaving you with a dark and hopeless feeling.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves strange indie horror and gross-out effects.
